Hello. Hello everybody. So I'm here with William, Mayor our Music Officer. I'll start off and
then we'll share the speaking notes. We do have a presentation and that's up there, so
we'll get started. Through the chair, we are pleased to bring forward the recommendation
of the City's 2026 Artist in Residence Appointment, which will focus on a musician in residence
opportunity. Through this call, we saw proposals from musicians, music educators, and music
entrepreneurs interested in delivering innovative, community-engaged music programming that would
create meaningful musical experiences for Kitchener residents of any age. Particular consideration
was given to proposals that demonstrated strong community connections, artistic merit, feasibility,
and the potential to create lasting impact within the Kitchener community.
To support applicants, staff hosted a series of information sessions
and provided additional support through phone and email consultations throughout the application period.
We received 13 eligible submissions from a strong and diverse pool of applicants.
Applications were evaluated by a jury consisting of an arts and culture advisory committee representative
and to music industry professionals.
Following a very thorough review process,
the jury is recommending Amanda Bram
for appointment as the 2026 Artist-in-Residence.
Amanda Bram is a Kitchener-based singer-songwriter,
multi-instrumentalist,
and producer with extensive experience
as a performer, educator, songwriter,
and emerging music therapist.
Her accomplishments include the release of two albums, recognition through several
provincial songwriting and performance competitions, and recent selection to
Via Rail's Artists On Board Program. Amanda's experience extends beyond
performance and includes community music initiatives, music education, and
collaborative songwriting processes designed to engage participants of
varying musical backgrounds and abilities. I've got a quick video here of Amanda's
participation in what's known as the Lullaby Project which pairs Amanda or

Amanda's proposed residency entitled Words of Wisdom and Hopes for the Future seeks to
bring together youth aged 13 to 18 and older adults aged 65 and over through the co-creation
of original songs, an intergenerational songwriting experience.
Participants will engage in guided songwriting sessions exploring themes of wisdom, lived
experience, aspirations, and future generations. The residency will culminate in a community
concert where participants will perform the original works alongside Amanda as well as
other supporting local musicians. The jury was particularly impressed by the proposal's
emphasis on intergenerational connection, community building, accessibility, and relationship
development through music. It is my pleasure to introduce the recommended 2026 Artisan
